description: Argus Transfer is framework that provides routing for named pipes inspired by the HTTP 1.1 request/response protocol that runs over named pipes layer.
releaseNotes:
[Add] ArgusProblemDetails: structured error responses in the style of RFC 7807 Problem Details; #29
            [Add] ArgusRetryPolicy: optional automatic retry of transient named pipe failures in ArgusClient; #30
            [Add] Global exception handling middleware, ArgusExceptionHandlerMiddleware; #31
            [Add] Content-Encoding support for compressed request and response bodies (gzip); #34
            [Add] Authorization header convention for process identity; #35
            [Add] Built-in authentication middleware with pluggable handlers; #36
            [Add] ArgusPipeHostOptions.MaxRequestHeaderSize: a limit on the size of the header block; #64
            [Add] ArgusPipeHostOptions.RequestReadTimeout and MaxConcurrentConnections: a request read timeout and a connection limit for the pipe host; #65
            [Add] ArgusClient.MaxResponseBodySize: an optional maximum response body size on the client; #76
            [Add] ArgusPipeHostOptions.ResponseWriteTimeout, so a client that does not read its response cannot hold a connection; #85
            [Change] Behavior change: ArgusPipeHostOptions validates its values when they are set, so an invalid limit, timeout or PipeName fails at startup with an exception that names the option; use 0 for no body size limit and Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan for no timeout; #67
            [Change] Behavior change: the host answers only request-format violations with 400, through ArgusProtocolException; other failures are server faults; #63
            [Change] Behavior change: routes are percent-encoded on the wire and decoded by the host, so a client and a host of different versions disagree on a route that contains %; header names and values are validated; #69
            [Change] Behavior change: route templates are validated at registration, so a mistyped template fails at startup instead of never matching; #73
            [Change] Behavior change: the response serializer is negotiated from the Accept header, and a new ArgusRequest no longer sets Accept: text/plain; without an Accept header the host uses its default serializer; #75
            [Change] Behavior change: the host's built-in 400, 406 and 503 responses are problem details (application/problem+json) instead of plain text; #77
            [Change] Behavior change: the protocol version in request and status lines is validated; anything other than ARGUS/1.0 is rejected; #81
            [Change] Route templates are parsed and middleware pipelines composed once, instead of for every request; #74
            [Change] ArgusClient.SendAsync leaves the caller's request unchanged and validates it; #79
            [Change] Documented why IArgusClient is IDisposable and what ArgusClient.Dispose does; #82
            [Change] The sample project demonstrates the current feature set and is tested end to end; #57
            [Update] Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions and Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions to version 10.0.12
            [Fix] Byte-safe message framing for non-ASCII and binary bodies; #33
            [Fix] A pipeline that completes without a response is answered with a generic 500 instead of a closed connection; #62
            [Fix] The client reads the response while writing the request, so an early rejection by the host does not deadlock; #68
            [Fix] The pipe accept loop keeps running after an unexpected exception; #70
            [Fix] Shutdown resources are disposed only after all requests have finished; #71
            [Fix] AddArgusModules can no longer scan the wrong assembly; #72
            [Fix] A null query parameter value is written as an empty value; #78
            [Fix] ArgusLoggingMiddleware logs a completion entry when the pipeline throws; #80
title: Argus Transfer
